data_notes: This dataset contains caption, URL, and owner metadata only. No likes, comments, or view counts were exported. Engagement multipliers cannot be calculated. Top performers and opening formula scores are derived from hook-type strategic signal and caption depth as proxies. Treat all multiplier values as illustrative estimates, not measured data.
285 creators appear with only 1 post — baseline calculations for these accounts are not possible. 47 creators appear with 2 posts — thin baseline, directional only.
Audio metadata was not included in the export. Audio trends section returns empty array.
Format detection is URL-based (/reel/ vs /p/). No carousel vs single-image distinction is possible from this data — all non-reel posts are grouped as Image/Carousel.

saturated.sub: Scene-setting captions with no perspective or insight make up 75% of posts — the most crowded and undifferentiated content type in the niche.
Wide-room and bed-with-light shots dominate Hotel & Accommodation posts with little narrative specificity or photographer POV.
Comment-for-link posts are heavily concentrated in a few large accounts and create noise that conditions audiences to scroll past.
Day-by-day travel itineraries are the most replicated format in Travel & Destination — high volume, diminishing return on attention.

underused.sub: Only a handful of accounts explore what makes a space photographable — an open lane that positions the creator as an expert, not just a guest.
Wellness properties appear in fewer than 1% of posts, yet natural light and spa settings are a natural fit for Natalie's aesthetic and client targets.
Showing the client brief, shot list planning, or art direction process has near-zero representation despite strong strategic interest signals.
London properties are deeply underrepresented relative to Italy, France, and Spain — a clear gap given Natalie's emerging London residency positioning.

hooks.text: "Most hotel photos show you a room. The ones that book rooms make you feel like you're already in it."
hooks.rationale: Models the contrarian reframe pattern seen in @ulterior_visuals and @lina.michy — the highest-performing hook type in this dataset. Positions Natalie as someone who understands the commercial function of photography, not just the aesthetic one. Speaks directly to her hotel and hospitality clients without naming them.

hooks.text: "Light in a hotel room has about 20 minutes of magic. Here's how I find it before the housekeeping cart gets there."
hooks.rationale: Draws from the curiosity-gap + authority pattern used by @roberta.dallalba and @cmcg.creative — specific process, sensory detail, and a twist that makes it feel earned. Natural light as a deliberate craft choice is central to Natalie's brand, and 'before the housekeeping cart' is concrete enough to feel real, not generic.

hooks.text: "There's a window in this suite that turns golden at 6:47am. We built the whole shoot around it."
hooks.rationale: Scene-setting with a specific detail (time, precision) that signals professional intent rather than tourist enthusiasm. Inspired by the atmospheric POV style of @relaischateaux and @sofikulin, but anchored in photographer craft rather than travel aspiration. The specificity is what separates this from the saturated 'golden hour' content type.

Engagement baseline: median interactions across all posts per creator in the bi-weekly dataset. Multiplier = post interactions ÷ creator median.
